best_wedge.workflow: In-company customs tariff classification: the historical classification log (new SKU or part to commodity code, per destination country) at one importer plus one licensed customs broker, including specialist escalations, broker-importer code disagreements and post-entry corrections. Geography: US (HTSUS, CBP CROSS) first, with one UK or EU importer (ATaR / BTI, France under the EU BTI regime as RTC) among the discovery targets.
best_wedge.why:
EVIDENCE LIMITATION FIRST. Nothing in this section is a measurement of category H anywhere; every H share in the project is an estimate, every volume and cost figure from a regulator, association, press or vendor site is unverified because those hosts were blocked and the search budget was exhausted, and the only primary artefacts read were GitHub-hosted (HMRC ATaR source code, Avalara SDK, the CBP CROSS scrape). The wedge is chosen on access cost and testability, not on evidence that it works; the ranker's prior for it is 5-15% H and the executive call is evidence against.

Why this workflow and not another: (1) The historical corpus already exists in structured form and can be exported without instrumenting anything. Avalara's ItemModel carries itemCode, description, itemGroup, category, a classifications list of {productCode, systemCode, country, isPremium}, createdUserId, modifiedUserId, createdDate, modifiedDate, source, and an hsCodeClassificationStatus list of {country, status, details, createdAt, completedAt, createdUserId} (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avadev/AvaTax-REST-V2-DotNet-SDK/main/src/models/ItemModel.cs and ItemHSCodeClassificationStatusModel.cs, vendor SDK source, fetched this session); its bulk classification jobs carry a TariffCodeNeedsReview criterion (ClassificationCriteriaModel.cs, same SDK), so a review queue exists as a data object. Equivalent exports from ONESOURCE, Descartes, SAP GTS or Oracle GTM are unverified (vendor docs blocked). Brokers hold classification worksheets for many importers at once, so one broker relationship yields several logs. (2) A public precedent corpus is reachable today for the external check: 216,164 dated CBP rulings with relatedRulings, modifies, revokes and tariffs columns (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justinmoonjeli/CROSSFetch/main/cbp_rulings_data.csv, open-source scrape of a government database; my recomputation this session: 20.9% cite a related ruling, 1.41% ever modified or revoked, 99.0% of 2023-24 rulings sit on a 6-digit line with a prior ruling and 89.1% on a 10-digit line with a prior ruling, 114 of 5,193 six-digit lines account for half of all ruling line mentions; the verifier's 77-line figure used a first-tariff-only method). HMRC's ATaR Decision record (bindingCommodityCode, effectiveStartDate, effectiveEndDate, justification, goodsDescription, methodSearch, methodCommercialDenomination, methodExclusion, appeal, cancellation; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hmrc/binding-tariff-classification/main/app/uk/gov/hmrc/bindingtariffclassification/model/Decision.scala, government source code, fetched) is a ready-made template for what a settlement record must contain, so the coding protocol can test whether company records carry any of those fields. (3) The decision owner also holds rule-making power over the object being settled: a head of trade compliance can set the company classification position for a product family and instruct brokers, which the falsification verifier named as condition (i) for any base-rate experiment; in mortgage (GSE guide), claims (courts, FOS), regulatory reporting (EBA) and ERISA (named fiduciary) the buyer does not own the meaning. (4) The decisions are classifications and approvals, not adverse decisions about individuals, so the H4 constraints (clinician review, fiduciary review, GDPR Art. 22, EU AI Act Annex III) do not apply; condition (ii) of the same verifier. (5) Class granularity is anchored by a public taxonomy (6-digit HS lines), so the recurrence test has an objective class key rather than a coder-invented one; condition (iii). (6) The outcome is a code plus effective dates, already executable in the item master, so a settlement can be made deterministic without replacing a system of record. (7) The incumbent gap is documented, even if narrow: Avalara's TaxRuleModel has effectiveDate, endDate, description, user stamps and no rationale field, and justification exists only as a premium free-text attachment (TaxRuleModel.cs, ClassificationModel.cs, ItemPremiumClassificationOutputModel.cs, verified by the cluster verifier); nothing links a settlement to like items.

What the wedge is not: it is not a market-size argument. Public loop volume is small (1,833 to 2,138 CBP rulings a year in 2021-2024, my recomputation of the same scrape), the observable pattern at CBP is a fresh human decision per product on already-ruled lines (B/A dominance), and the honest prior is that the experiment returns a single-digit to low-teens H share and kills the wedge. It is chosen because it is the cheapest place to get a real answer.
best_wedge.access_to_historical_cases: Cheap and structured, subject to one willing company. Sources, in order of preference: (a) GTM item master export with the Avalara-equivalent fields above (itemCode, description, itemGroup, category, classifications per country, created and modified user and date, HS classification status with details and completedAt); (b) the team's classification worksheet or spreadsheet, which at many importers is the real record (inference, unverified); (c) escalation emails or tickets and broker classification requests for a 12-month window; (d) broker-importer disagreement records and broker instruction letters; (e) post-entry corrections, protests and reconciliation adjustments traced to classification (HMRC models this regulator-side as a LiabilityOrder case with traderCommodityCode vs officerCommodityCode, Application.scala in the same repo, government source code); (f) the company classification manual or family templates with version history; (g) binding ruling requests and outcomes. External check at zero access cost: the CROSS CSV locally and the HMRC public ATaR search (gov.uk blocked in this session but public). No regulator access is needed. What cannot be obtained without a company: any of (a) to (g); public corpora sample the ruled tail and cannot give the base rate (falsification verifier H1-H4). A broker is the best first source because one brokerage holds worksheets for many importers and prices classification per line, which also anchors cost per decision.
best_wedge.access_to_decision_owners: One named role per company and it already buys tooling: Director or Head of Global Trade Compliance, Customs Compliance Manager, or Classification Lead at importers; Licensed Customs Broker or Classification Manager at brokerages. The role is identifiable by title on LinkedIn and through broker and trade compliance associations (NCBFAA, ICPA, AAEI; [RECALL, unverified] as recruiting channels). Whether the role's budget is separable from the GTM contract and broker fees is unknown and is a discovery question, not an assumption. The role is also the natural adjudicator for the base-rate experiment and the person who can say, per case, whether they would ratify a reading as a family position.
best_wedge.why_not_the_larger_markets: Mortgage underwriting help desk: larger labour pool ([RECALL, unverified] several million originations a year) but the lender cannot make a reading of the Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac or FHA guide authoritative, the owners already encode the largest interpretive area themselves (income calculators with rep-and-warrant relief, DU and LPA; recall), overlays are risk appetite (E) not settlements, the log is email with no structured export, every volume figure is recall, and FHA Refer files require manual underwriting by rule (H4). Merchant underwriting at a PSP: single owner and versioned restricted lists are attractive, but the queue lives in in-house tooling with no export pattern examined, PSP access is harder than broker access, the verifier's own kill line is class-level H above 15-20% at thousands of cases a year with zero data, and any result becomes a feature of the onboarding tool. KYC/CDD exceptions: 100% human by definition but volumes guessed at hundreds to low thousands per bank, a documented rationale is expected per exception (H4 risk), and Fenergo, Encompass and Alloy own the policy rules. P&C claims coverage referrals: the largest processor pool (365,300 US adjusters, BLS snippet) but the settled object is owned externally (courts, FOS fair-and-reasonable, FCA v Arch), and wording interpretation is 2.6% of upheld FOS cases and 1.2% of 1,349 claim decisions (third-party regex corpus, weak). Regulatory reporting interpretation: sector recurrence is sourced (69.7% of EBA Q&As in classes asked twice or more) but the EBA owns the meaning, runs the store free, and finals fell to 54 in 2025. Lloyd's delegated authority: a good single interview, not a base-rate experiment; special acceptances are non-precedential by design and the binder endorsement already exists as the versioned instrument. In every one of these the buyer either lacks rule-making power over the settled object, faces a human-review mandate on the decision, or cannot hand over a structured log; customs classification is the only shortlisted workflow that clears all three access tests.

competitive_threat.shape: feature inside an existing workflow product
competitive_threat.reasoning: On the verified record the unshipped piece is a field set and a link, not a system. Avalara already stores the settled code per country with user and date stamps, an effective-dated executable TaxRule override, a review-queue criterion and a premium free-text justification (SDK source, fetched). The missing objects are structured facts relied on, the rule reading, the ratifying authority, an applicability scope to like items and a version pointer, which is the same increment ServiceNow (exception record with requester, approver, validity dates, sys_audit, retired document versions, case-to-knowledge) and Marble (RuleSnooze with creator, source decision, rule, pivot, start and expiry; LLM case reviewer over prior cases) have already shipped in their own domains (vendor docs mirror and open-source vendor code, fetched by the H5-H8 and payments verifiers). Every institution examined that runs a settlement loop built it itself (HMRC ATaR, CBP CROSS, EBA, GSEs, Visa CE3.0), and the one open-source interpretation ledger built for this artefact class parked itself for lack of demand (PubLedge INTENT.md, 0 stars, weak signal). H5 makes any corpus single-tenant, and H7 makes it exportable as tables, so a standalone vendor has no data moat and must win on process adoption and integrations, which the item-master owner already has. The consulting or service layer is the second most likely shape: classification is already sold per line by brokers and by Avalara as a service, so a broker or advisory firm could run a ledger for its clients as part of the fee. Standalone survives only if the experiment shows H above the economic gate at companies that use several GTM systems or none, and GTM vendors decline to add the fields; 'not built at all' is the live outcome if the base-rate experiment returns single-digit H, which is the prior.
competitive_threat.who_would_absorb_it: Item-master and GTM owners first: Avalara (AvaTax items, classifications, TaxRule, Classification MCP server and premium justification, all evidenced in SDK or docs on GitHub), Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE Global Classification, Descartes CustomsInfo, E2open Global Knowledge, SAP GTS and Oracle GTM (feature sets unverified, vendor sites blocked). Second, customs brokers and forwarder brokerage arms as a service layer, because they already hold classification worksheets for many importers and price per line ([RECALL, unverified] for pricing practice). Third, on the public side, the authorities themselves: HMRC ships the loop as open-source software and is building AI drafting with review and provenance in-house (finder, from the HMRC repos), and CBP publishes supersession links in CROSS. Agent platforms (AWS AgentCore Cedar generation, Microsoft AGT approvals) would absorb the generic 'settle once, enforce after' primitive if the product were framed as a control plane rather than a customs feature.

research_gaps: The share of a live in-company classification queue that is repeatable settleable ambiguity (categories 7 and 8) versus missing facts and per-item factual classification. No public source exists; no live review pool in any domain was split facts-versus-interpretation by any finder or verifier. Only a company log can supply it.

Annual classification volume per company (new SKUs or parts, times destination countries) and the share routed to a specialist or escalated. Avalara's bulk-job counters (classified, inProgress, notClassified, failed) show the queue exists but no rate is published; EU BTI and UK ATaR annual counts are blocked and CBP volume is only the public tail.

Cost per classification decision and per escalation: internal specialist hours, broker per-line fees, ruling-request and counsel costs. The only figure found (1 to 4 hours per item) is from a 33-entry hobby README and carries near-zero weight; BLS wage data for the role is blocked and any figure used is recall.

Where settled readings actually live (GTM item master, broker files, spreadsheets, email, classification manual) and whether they are ever retrieved before a new decision; the CROSS methodSearch analogue exists at HMRC but nothing shows in-company search behaviour.

Rework attributable to inconsistent application of an existing in-house position: post-entry corrections, protests, reconciliation adjustments and broker-importer disagreements per year, and what share trace to a prior settlement not being applied rather than new facts. CBP penalty data (19 USC 1592), HMRC liability caseload and ECA misclassification findings are all blocked.

Whether ONESOURCE Global Classification, Descartes CustomsInfo, E2open, SAP GTS and Oracle GTM already carry rationale, approval, applicability and version objects on classifications. Only Avalara's open SDK was inspected; the others are unverified because vendor documentation is blocked.

Whether the trade compliance lead in fact ratifies family-level positions in a form that binds brokers and group entities, and how often the same interpretive question returns after such a ratification. Structural only; no interview evidence.

Willingness to pay, budget line and procurement path: whether classification tooling budget is separable from the GTM contract and broker fees, and whether the buyer would take a point tool at all. No pricing, ACV or sales-cycle evidence exists for any shortlisted workflow.

Duty and penalty exposure attributable to misclassification at a target company, and the share of it caused by inconsistency rather than by a wrong first reading. Needed to know whether risk avoided can substitute for labour savings in the payback case.

Cross-company recurrence of the same interpretive families (sets, parts versus accessories, essential character, chapter-note exclusions), which decides whether any content is shareable across customers (H5). Public rulings show family recurrence at 6-digit level but nothing shows two companies settling the same question the same way.

Durability of settlements against schedule changes: how often HTS or CN amendments invalidate an in-house position and how the company discovers affected items. CROSS shows 1.41% lifetime supersession on the public side only; company-side invalidation is unmeasured.

Whether deterministic application of an in-house reading changes the importer's reasonable-care posture or audit outcome; customs counsel and CBP Focused Assessment practice are recall only (ecfr.gov, cbp.gov blocked).

Robinson; named as types, not as evidence they will participate)

One consumer electronics or connected-device importer (multi-function goods, principal function questions)

One GTM vendor product team (Avalara, Descartes, ONESOURCE or SAP GTS) to test H6 directly
One customs and trade law firm (tests whether in-house positions are ratified, contested and how 'we settled this before' plays at CBP or HMRC)
questions: Walk me through the last new SKU or part that took more than one working day to classify. What was the hold-up: a missing spec, sample or vendor description, determining what the product is, or disagreement about what a rule means?

How many new items did your team classify in the last 12 months, and into how many destination countries? How many went to a specialist or were escalated, and how do you define escalated in your system?

Where does a classification decision live once made: item master, spreadsheet, broker's system, email? Does the record hold why the code was chosen, which facts were relied on, who approved it, and which other items it applies to, or only the code, user and date?
When a new product resembles something you classified before, how do you find the prior decision, how often do you find it, and how often do you re-decide anyway?

Name three interpretive questions your team settled in the last two years, for example parts versus accessories for a family, whether an assortment is a set, essential character for a product line. Who settled each, in what form, were brokers instructed, and has the same question come back since?
How often do you and your broker disagree on a code? What happens next, and is there a log?

In the last 12 months how many post-entry corrections, protests, reconciliation adjustments or duty refund claims traced to classification? Of those, how many were cases where you had already decided the question but it was applied differently?
Have you requested a binding ruling (CBP, ATaR, BTI) in the last three years? For what fraction of your interpretive questions, and why not more often?
Who has authority to set a company classification position, and does it bind all entities and countries or only one?
What does a classification cost you: internal hours per item and per escalation, broker per-line fees, counsel? Which budget line pays for classification tooling and who signs?
What does your GTM vendor already do for rationale, approval, applicability and version history of classifications? What have you asked them for and what did they say?

If, at the moment of classifying a new item, a tool showed 'this question was settled on date X by Y for family Z, here is the reading and the facts it relied on', what would you do with it, and what would make you distrust or ignore it?
How many people classify, and roughly how is their time split between gathering facts and deciding?
How often do HTS or CN schedule changes invalidate a prior position, and how do you find the affected items?

Escalation emails or tickets and broker classification requests for the same 12 months, or a random sample of 50 with attachments
Broker instruction letters or classification guidance sent to brokers, with dates
Internal classification manual or family templates with version history
List of binding ruling requests and outcomes in the last three years

Headcount and time allocation of the classification team, and broker per-line fee schedule
GTM contract scope and price band (for anchoring the plausible price), and any vendor roadmap correspondence on rationale or approval fields
A sample of 20 escalated cases with all attachments, for the pilot coding
supporting_answers: Escalations number in the thousands a year at the company, or the broker's pooled queue does, and the interviewee describes a material share of them as arguments about what a rule means rather than about facts
The same interpretive question is described as returning within a year and being re-decided, with brokers or other entities deciding it differently
Settled readings live in email, spreadsheets or people's heads, brokers are not instructed, and the item master holds only the code, user and date
Post-entry corrections or broker disagreements are traced by the interviewee to inconsistent application of something already decided, not to new facts
One named owner ratifies family-level positions, would bind brokers and entities, and would sign for a tool from a budget line that is not the GTM contract
The GTM vendor product manager confirms there is no structured rationale, approval or applicability object on classifications and none on the roadmap
At least one company agrees within two weeks to export the log under NDA for the base-rate experiment
killing_answers: Most delay is spec sheets, samples and vendor descriptions; specialists spend most time gathering facts (H1)
Escalations are in the low hundreds a year or fewer, or the team classifies thousands of items with almost no escalation because family templates and vendor auto-classification handle them (H2, H8)
Even within a family every item is a fresh factual decision ('every garment is different'), so prior readings do not remove work (category 3 dominance)
Prior decisions are found through the item group and copied without re-deciding; the process already works (H3)
Settled readings already sit in ONESOURCE, Descartes, SAP GTS or Avalara with approval and version history (H3, H6)
The owner declines to make positions binding on brokers or entities, or says every interpretive question is resolved by requesting a ruling (H4, owner is the authority)
Tooling budget is the GTM contract and the buyer says they would only take this as a GTM or broker feature (H6)
No company will share a log even under NDA with a free audit in return; the wedge is then untestable and should be dropped
discovery_sprint.sequencing_and_recruiting: Week 1: the two brokers first. They hold worksheets for many importers, speak the vocabulary needed to write the codebook, and their per-line fee gives the cost anchor for the thresholds; ask each for referrals to two importer clients with large new-item flows. Weeks 2 to 3: the five importers, recruited through broker referrals, LinkedIn title search on the exact titles above, and trade compliance associations ([RECALL, unverified] NCBFAA, ICPA, AAEI directories); include one UK or EU importer. Week 3: the marketplace and the GTM vendor product manager, after the importer interviews so that the vendor conversation tests specific claims. Week 4: the attorney last, armed with the interviewees' descriptions of ratified positions and disputes. Offer every company a free classification-consistency audit (the coded sample and a short report) under NDA in exchange for the log export; pay brokers for their time; do not recruit through vendor channels, which would bias toward companies already well tooled. The go or no-go for the base-rate experiment is taken after interview six: unless at least one company has agreed to export a log, the wedge is untestable and the project should record that as its result. Record every interview claim as unverified until the log confirms it; interview claims about escalation share and recurrence are the hypotheses the experiment tests, not evidence.

base_rate_experiment.sample: 300 to 500 classification decisions per company from one to three companies, at least one importer and one broker, drawn from a single 12-month window. Two strata per company: (i) a random 150 to 200 from all classification decisions in the window, to measure the all-decision share of categories 7 and 8; (ii) all escalated or specialist-reviewed decisions in the window if 300 or fewer, otherwise a random 200 to 300, to measure the escalation share, which is the addressable pool. If the company cannot identify escalations, use a stated proxy and report it: decisions where completedAt minus createdAt exceeds one working day, decisions where modifiedUserId differs from createdUserId, or decisions carrying the vendor's needs-review status. Stratify (ii) by product family so that no single family exceeds 25% of the sample. Precision: at n = 400 and a true share of 15% the 95% binomial interval is about plus or minus 3.5 points; at n = 200 per stratum about plus or minus 5 points, enough to separate 8% from 15% from 25%, which are the decision boundaries below. Exclude items auto-classified with no human touch from stratum (ii) but count them in stratum (i) as category 1 candidates.
base_rate_experiment.source_of_cases: Primary: the company's GTM item master export with the Avalara-equivalent fields (itemCode, description, itemGroup, category, classifications {productCode, systemCode, country, isPremium}, createdUserId, modifiedUserId, createdDate, modifiedDate, hsCodeClassificationStatus {country, status, details, createdAt, completedAt}; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/avadev/AvaTax-REST-V2-DotNet-SDK/main/src/models/ItemModel.cs, vendor SDK source) or the equivalent from ONESOURCE, Descartes, SAP GTS or Oracle GTM (field sets unverified). Joined to: the team's classification worksheet, escalation emails or tickets, broker classification requests and instruction letters, the classification manual or family templates with version history, ruling requests, and the post-entry correction and protest log. External precedent lookup per case: the CROSS scrape (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/justinmoonjeli/CROSSFetch/main/cbp_rulings_data.csv, open-source scrape, 216,164 dated rulings with tariffs, relatedRulings, modifies and revokes columns) filtered to rulings dated before the decision date on the same 6-digit and 10-digit line, and the HMRC public ATaR search for UK cases. For each sampled decision the team assembles a decision packet: description and spec available at decision time, code assigned per country, who and when, whether a prior in-house item in the same family existed at that date and what code it carried, whether a public ruling on the same line and question existed at that date, whether the case was escalated and any recorded reason, and any later correction. The HMRC Decision record (justification, methodSearch, methodCommercialDenomination, methodExclusion, effective dates, cancellation; Decision.scala, government source code) is the checklist of what a settlement record would need to contain; the packet records which of those elements the company record actually holds.
base_rate_experiment.coding_protocol: Two coders code every packet independently and blind to each other, assigning one primary category and at most one secondary category, plus a class key. Coding proceeds through an ordered decision tree so that categories are mutually exclusive by construction: Q1 Was a fact required by the schedule (composition, fibre content, function, material predominance, sample, spec) absent at the time, causing a request, hold or delay? If yes, primary 2. Q2 With the facts on file, could the coder reproduce the code in under five minutes using only the schedule notes and the company's existing family template or a prior same-family decision, with no judgment call? If yes, primary 1. Q3 Was the human work determining what the product is (essential character among components, principal function, predominant material) under a rule whose meaning was not in dispute, such that a different product in the same family would need the same per-item work? If yes, primary 3. Q4 Did the decision turn on what a rule text means (scope of 'parts', 'sets put up for retail sale', a chapter-note exclusion, GIR 3(b) as a rule)? If yes, go to Q5; if no, go to Q7. Q5 Had the company already settled that question for the same family before this decision date, evidenced by a dated prior decision, template, memo or broker instruction the coder can cite? If yes, primary 7, and record whether the prior settlement was applied consistently or re-decided or contradicted. If no, Q6 Does the record show an authorised person stating the reading in family-general terms intended to govern future items (memo, template update, broker instruction, item-group rule)? If yes, primary 8; if the reading exists only in this item's record, primary 5. Q7 Did two authorities or rules point to different codes (NY versus HQ ruling, EU versus UK, company template versus public ruling, broker versus importer instruction) and the decision resolved which prevails? If yes, primary 6. Q8 Otherwise, if the company chose among defensible codes on risk or commercial grounds for this shipment with no intent to govern other items (taking the lower-duty code pending a ruling, deferring to the broker), primary 4. Anything left is coded 3 with a flag for review. Class key for 7 and 8: the 6-digit line or company product family, times the interpretive question type, for example '8708 brackets: parts of vehicles versus 7326 articles of iron'. Also recorded per case: whether a public ruling on the same 10-digit line and question existed at decision date (public duplication flag), the number of other sampled and unsampled items in the same class within the window (recurrence count), and time from creation to completion. Pilot: 30 cases from the escalation stratum coded first to test the codebook; codebook revised at most once; then the full sample.
base_rate_experiment.category_definitions: (1) Fully deterministic: with the facts on file at decision time, the GRIs, section and chapter notes and the company's existing family template or a prior same-family decision yield one code with no judgment call; a human touched it for entry or checking only. (2) Missing evidence: the decision was blocked or delayed because a fact the schedule needs (composition, fibre content, function, material breakdown, sample, spec sheet, vendor description) was absent; the analogue is HMRC's only coded referral reasons REQUEST_SAMPLE and REQUEST_MORE_INFO. (3) Factual classification: facts were available but establishing what the product is (essential character among components, principal function, material predominance by weight or value) required specialist reading of the spec against a rule whose meaning was not in question; the same rule applied to a different product needs the same per-item work. (4) One-off discretion: the company chose among defensible codes on risk or commercial grounds for this shipment, for example taking the lower-duty code pending a ruling or deferring to the broker, with no statement intended to govern other items. (5) Ambiguity of rule meaning, left case-specific: the decision turned on what a rule text means (scope of 'parts', 'sets', chapter-note exclusions, GIR 3(b) as a rule) and the record states no family-level reading. (6) Conflict between rules or authorities: two rulings, jurisdictions, instructions or templates pointed to different codes and the decision resolved which prevails. (7) Recurring previously-settled ambiguity: the interpretive question was already settled by the company for the same family before this decision date, evidenced by a citable dated record, and a human nonetheless re-decided it, or decided inconsistently with it; a case where the prior settlement was found and applied without re-deciding is coded 1 with the class key retained, because that is the working state the product claims to create. (8) New ambiguity settled prospectively: the interpretive question was new to the company and the record shows an authorised person stating the reading in family-general terms intended to govern future items; if the reading survives only in this item's record it is 5.
base_rate_experiment.coders_and_agreement: Coder A: a licensed customs broker or former trade compliance classification specialist on contract, not an employee of the company supplying the log. Coder B: a trained analyst without customs background, working from the codebook and ten worked examples, so that the codebook, not domain intuition, carries the categories. Both blind to each other and to the project's thesis framing (they receive category definitions, not the hypothesis). Pilot gate: on 30 escalation-stratum cases, Cohen's kappa at least 0.70 on the eight-way primary code and at least 0.75 on the binary (7 or 8 versus other). If not met, revise the codebook once and re-pilot on 30 fresh cases; if still not met, stop and report that facts and interpretation are not operationally separable in this workflow's records, which is itself a finding against the product (it means a captured settlement cannot be reliably matched to a new case). Full sample: report percentage agreement, kappa on both scales, each coder's shares for every category, and the adjudicated shares. Adjudicator: the company's trade compliance lead, shown the two codes without knowing which coder gave which, who also answers per category-8 case whether they did or would ratify the reading as a family position. The decision thresholds below apply to the lower of the two coders' pre-adjudication shares, not the adjudicated share, to prevent adjudication drift toward the thesis. For the prior IPSA study two coding passes reached kappa 0.78 to 1.0 on tribunal-type documents (prior_evidence.md, hash-verified primary PDFs), which sets the expectation for what is achievable on structured records.
base_rate_experiment.thresholds: All inputs below are estimates or recall; no cost, volume or price figure for this workflow was sourced in this project, and the gates must be recomputed with the interview values before the experiment is scored. Working model: annual escalation labour L = N times C, where N is escalated classification decisions a year and C is the loaded cost per escalation. Savings S = h times r times L, where h is the share of escalations in categories 7 plus 8 and r is the fraction of an H escalation's cost the product removes (the settled reading removes the interpretive step and the re-decision, not the fact gathering). Requirement: S at least 3P in year one, where P is the annual price, because a mid-market buyer will not pay for a point tool beside the GTM suite on less than roughly three-to-one verifiable labour savings, and risk avoided is not verifiable at sale (heuristic, estimate). Parameter values: C = $200 central, range $100 to $300 (estimate: one to three specialist hours at a loaded $75 to $100 an hour; wage data blocked, BLS compliance-officer pay is recall; the hobby README's 1 to 4 hours per item carries near-zero weight per the verifier). N = 2,500 central for a mid-size importer, range 500 to 5,000 (estimate, no source; a broker's pooled queue could exceed 10,000). r = 0.5 (estimate). P = $30,000 ACV (estimate; no GTM add-on pricing reachable). Result: required h = 3P divided by (r times N times C) = 90,000 divided by (0.5 times 2,500 times 200) = 36% at the central mid-size importer, which is above every H estimate in this project (5 to 15%). At N = 5,000 and C = $300, required h = 12%; at N = 10,000 and C = $300, 6%. Gates, in order. Gate 1, minimum frequency: categories 7 plus 8 at least 15% of the escalation stratum, and at least 5% of the all-decision stratum, by the lower coder. The 15% is the value at which a company with L of at least $1.2M a year (for example 5,000 escalations at $240) pays back; if the interviews show L below $1.2M at the target company, the required h rises as 90,000 divided by (0.5 times L) and that higher number is the gate, which at the central estimate means 36%. The 5% all-decision floor exists because if escalations are a small fraction of decisions the addressable pool is small regardless of h. Gate 2, minimum recurrence: at least 50% of category 7 plus 8 decisions fall in classes with three or more occurrences in the 12-month window (counting unsampled items in the same class), and no more than 40% of classes are singletons. Basis: recording a settlement with facts, reading, authority and scope costs the owner roughly one hour ($100, estimate) plus review, and each reuse saves r times C = $100, so break-even is one reuse and the compounding claim needs a median of three; the owner's own permission log (47.5% of settlements never reused, median two later calls, private data) is the prior for failure. Gate 3, capture failure: at least 50% of category 7 cases show the prior settlement was re-decided or contradicted rather than applied; if prior settlements were mostly found and applied, H3 holds and the product adds nothing. Gate 4, prospective ratification: at least one third of category 8 cases were ratified by the owner in family-general terms within the window; otherwise the readings are category 5 and the prospective claim fails for this company. Gate 5, public duplication: fewer than 50% of category 7 plus 8 settlements match a public ruling on the same 10-digit line and question at the decision date; otherwise the remedy is retrieval over the public corpus, which open-source classifiers already attempt, not a private ledger. Gate 6, effort: the 300 to 500 cases must be reconstructable from the export and attachments; if more than 20% of sampled cases lack enough record to code, the company's records are too thin for the product to run on either, and that is reported.
base_rate_experiment.decision_rule: Continue toward a product only if all six gates pass at two or more of the participating companies, or at one company whose measured L times h clears the payback requirement with the interview-supplied C and N, and the GTM vendor interview did not show the fields already exist. Pivot to a feature partnership or a broker-run service if h is between 8% and 15% of escalations by the lower coder, or if gates 1 to 4 pass in only one company, or if gate 5 fails (retrieval over public rulings is the need). Stop the standalone product if h is below 8% at every company, or gate 2 fails everywhere (settlements do not recur within a year), or gate 3 fails everywhere (prior settlements are already applied), or the pilot cannot reach the kappa gate after one revision, or no company will export a log within the sprint. Publish the coder-level shares with intervals, the gate values with the interview-supplied parameters, and the list of category 7 and 8 classes with their recurrence counts, so the decision can be audited against the pre-registered gates rather than against a narrative. The gates are fixed before coding begins and are not revised after the shares are known.
base_rate_experiment.what_it_cannot_decide: It cannot decide willingness to pay, the buyer's budget line, ACV or sales cycle; no purchase evidence exists and the payback model uses an estimated price. It cannot decide whether ONESOURCE, Descartes, SAP GTS or Oracle GTM already carry rationale, approval and version objects, because their documentation was unreachable; a positive experiment can still be a feature request to an incumbent. It cannot generalise beyond the one to three companies sampled (H5): a willing company with an organised log is likely not representative, and companies with the worst capture are least able to supply a log, so the sample is biased in an unknown direction. It cannot show that a captured settlement would have been found and applied at the moment of the next decision; retrospective coding measures recurrence and capture failure, not the effect of a tool, which needs a prospective trial. It cannot supply cost per escalation or escalations per year; those come from interviews and are self-reported. It cannot tell whether the company's settled readings are right in law: a consistently applied wrong code compounds duty and penalty exposure, and a company position is a risk stance, not a binding ruling, so the experiment says nothing about liability under reasonable-care obligations (ecfr.gov and cbp.gov blocked, recall only). It cannot measure durability against schedule changes beyond the window, and the public 1.41% supersession rate does not transfer to in-house positions. It cannot cleanly separate category 3 from 5 where the fact in question is itself a legal construct such as essential character; coder disagreement will expose this boundary but not resolve it, and the definitions treat it by rule order, which is a convention. It cannot estimate market size or the number of companies above the L threshold; it answers only whether the mechanism exists at a rate that could pay at the sampled companies. Finally, if the escalation stratum has to be defined by a proxy (time to completion, modified-by-another-user, needs-review status), the measured share is a share of the proxy pool, and comparisons across companies with different proxies are not valid.
